title: Garment unrest eases as workers return, but Ashulia stays tense
excerpt: Almost all factories in Gazipur reopened on 5 November. In Savar and Ashulia, more than 100 stayed shut and protests went on.
content:
Garment workers went back to work in most industrial areas around Dhaka on Thursday, 5 November, after nearly a week of protests over the minimum wage, The Daily Star reported on 6 November. Savar and Ashulia remained the exception.

Where things stand

  • Gazipur: production resumed at nearly all factories. Industrial police superintendent Amjad Hossain said “99.99 percent” were running.
  • Narayanganj: factories and traffic were back to normal, with extra security at Chashara.
  • Mirpur: no unrest was reported, and most factories reopened around 2pm.
  • Savar and Ashulia: more than 100 of the 1,863 factories declared holidays as a precaution. Protests went on and there were fresh clashes with police. Two factory gates were damaged at Dosaid.

Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has 33 platoons in the industrial areas and has started using drones to watch them, the newspaper reported.

The wage timeline

Workers want a minimum wage of Tk 30,000 a month, up from Tk 12,500. The government formed a six-member wage board on 1 November. At its first meeting on 4 November, the board said the new wage structure would take effect in December, and workers would get their first pay under it in January 2027. The amount has not been set.

One worker told the newspaper that people had heard about the wage board’s progress and “saw no reason to continue the protests”. A garment worker, Toufiq Hossain, 35, died of injuries suffered during the unrest, The Daily Star reported on 5 November.

Why it matters

Organisations working with garment workers in Savar and Ashulia should still plan around closures and a heavy security presence. Elsewhere, field work can resume, but the situation could change quickly if the wage board’s figure falls far short of workers’ demands.

What to watch

The date of the wage board’s next meeting, the first proposed figure, and what happens to the cases filed against protesters.

Sources

  • Garment unrest eases as workers return to work, The Daily Star, 6 November 2026
  • January hike pledge fails to quell RMG unrest, The Daily Star, 5 November 2026
